note: 12 claims: 7 confirmed, 3 corrected, 2 unverified; the new guide fixes most round 1 errors (authorize URLs, consent, sandbox, partner approval), but it still leaves out that refreshing returns no new refresh token, the HTTPS/localhost redirect rule, and the Terms acceptance at app creation.

rows.claim: Who can create a developer app
rows.composio: Needs Owner or Admin access to the Developer section.
rows.ours: Sign in (to the sandbox) as an admin and create the app in Developer settings.
rows.provider: "You need admin access to your Ramp dashboard"; go to Company → Developer.

rows.composio: Click Create new app, name it, and agree to the Developer Terms of Service.
rows.ours: Only 'Create the app in Developer settings'; no Create New App, naming or Terms acceptance step, and the step is marked agent-owned.
rows.provider: Company → Developer → "Create New App", name the app and accept the Terms; then copy the Client ID and Client Secret.

rows.claim: Grant types must be enabled on the app
rows.composio: Enable Authorization code, Client credentials and Refresh token.
rows.ours: Enable Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants; refresh tokens are issued only if the Refresh Token grant is enabled.
rows.provider: "To get refresh tokens, enable the Refresh Token grant type for your app"; a grant that isn't enabled makes the request fail.

rows.claim: Partner or production approval for multi-customer apps
rows.ours: Partner-gated: a partner application, then a production access application; review time not published.
rows.provider: "Approval is required before production access"; Ramp reviews integration flows (stages: Build, Apply for Production Access, Beta Testing, Public Listing). No review time stated.

rows.composio: Add URIs in the app's Redirect URIs section, and they must match exactly.
rows.ours: Callback URL must exactly match a configured URI, including the path; HTTPS/localhost rule not mentioned.
rows.provider: "Must exactly match a redirect URI configured for your app, including the path"; must be HTTPS, with HTTP allowed only for localhost or 127.0.0.1.

rows.composio: Lists accounting, bills, cards, business, users, vendors and receipts scopes, plus offline_access.
rows.ours: resource:permission format; transactions:read, business:read; cards:read_vault restricted to approved integrators; partner-only scopes only in partner console.
rows.provider: Scopes follow resource:permission (OIDC scopes openid/offline_access excepted); "cards:read_vault is available only to approved integrators"; partner-only scopes appear only in the partner Developer Console.

rows.ours: Access tokens last 1 hour by default; exchange the code within 5 minutes. Refresh token lifetime/rotation not covered.
rows.provider: Auth Code/Refresh access tokens default to 1 hour (use expires_in); codes expire after 5 minutes (docs now say 5, not 10); refreshing returns no new refresh token and doesn't extend its lifetime.

rows.composio: The Authorization URL differs between demo and production.
rows.ours: Sandbox https://demo.ramp.com/v1/authorize, production https://app.ramp.com/v1/authorize, with a state value.

rows.composio: Demo and production accounts use different base and authorization URLs.
rows.ours: Separate sandbox and production apps; tokens work only in the issuing environment; sandbox uses demo.ramp.com / demo-api.ramp.com.
rows.provider: "Sandbox and production need separate apps"; "Tokens work only in the environment that issued them"; sandbox API base is demo-api.ramp.com.

rows.claim: Who can approve the consent screen
rows.ours: Admin or Business Owner must approve whole-business apps; user-level apps need an admin to enable them in Manage Access first.
rows.provider: Whole-business apps need an Admin or Business Owner to approve; for user-level apps "an admin must first enable the app for the organization in Manage Access".

rows.ours: Listed as an open question: PKCE support not stated in the pages read.
rows.provider: The authorization guide doesn't mention PKCE; the changelog (June 22, 2026) only adds an optional code_challenge (S256) to the application OAuth handoff authorize params, so support for the standard flow isn't settled.

rows.claim: Email verification when creating an app
rows.composio: A 6-digit email code is required, valid for 5 minutes.
rows.provider: Ramp's getting-started guide and changelog don't mention any email verification code for app creation.
